newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron sees Indian project back on course.
newsitem.headline: Enron sees Indian project back on course.

text.p: Enron Corporation said on Monday it was pleased with the decision of a Bombay court to dismiss the only remaining lawsuit filed against its Dabhol Power Company.
"This is the last critical step in getting the Dabhol Power Project back on track for completion by December 1998," Kenneth Lay, Enron's chairman and CEO said in a statement.
Earlier in the day, the Bombay High Court dismissed a petition seeking to stop Enron from pursuing its Dabhhol power project on India's western coast.
Judges D.P. Saraf and M.S. Rane of a division bench of the high court dismissed the petition which sought scrapping of Dabhol Power Company's power project alleging irregularities.
The petition was filed by the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU).
"Preliminary site preparation activities are underway and construction should be fully activated within a week of execution of financing documents," Lay said.

Enron has already faced and won over 20 law suits against its power project. Dabhol Power Company is 80 percent owned by Enron Development Corp and 10 percent each by U.S. firms Bechtel and General Electric.
